newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile resort opposes Los Pelambres copper port.
newsitem.headline: Chile resort opposes Los Pelambres copper port.

text.p: Residents of Chilean seaside resort Los Vilos opposed on Monday plans by the owners of the Los Pelambres copper mine to build a port near the town, saying it would damage beaches and threaten fishing facilities.

"Los Vilos manifest its most energetic rejection of the building on its beaches of a maritime terminal to ship mineral concentrate from the Luksic group property," said the statement from the Committee for the Defence of the San Pedro fishing harbour at Los Vilos.
The company plans to build a port and plant to extract water from the concentrates at Punta Chungo three kilometers north of Los Vilos on Chile's central Pacific coast.
The protest from Los Vilos follows the release of the project's environment impact study for approval by the authorities and public comment.
The mine's owners are planning to invest over $1 billion in expanding the pit's output from 23,000 tonnes to over 260,000 tonnes a year.
Los Pelambres is owned by the Luksic goup and a Japanese consortium led by Mitsubishi and Nippon Mining.
